Another major step in the government’s plan to list all Coal India subsidiaries by 2030 | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
Coal India subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) on Monday fixed a price band of ₹129-136 per equity share for its approximately ₹9,000-crore initial public offering (IPO), marking another major step in the government’s plan to list all Coal India subsidiaries by 2030.
The IPO, entirely an offer for sale (OFS), will see Coal India offload around 66.2 crore equity shares, representing a 10% stake in its Sambalpur-headquartered subsidiary. The bidding window will open on November 19 and close on November 23.
MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes (MT) of coal in FY26. It accounts for approximately 21% of India’s domestic coal production. The company operates 17 mines, including 14 opencast and three underground mines.
MCL reported a net profit of ₹4,880.66 crore during the six months ended September 30, while revenue stood at ₹16,093.04 crore.
The proposed listing is part of the government’s broader strategy to unlock value in Coal India’s subsidiaries through public listings and widen investor participation in the country’s coal sector.
South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL) and NLC India’s renewable energy arm, NLC India Renewables Ltd (NIRL), are also expected to make their stock market debuts during the current fiscal.
